static_traits.name: Zhang Cheng
static_traits.family_status: Became a grandparent at 44; has one grandchild
static_traits.medical_history: Has not experienced similar problems before; has not received psychotherapy; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly cooperative, negative tone; showing cognitive tendencies like catastrophizing, negating the positive, mental filtering, mind reading, predicting the future, overgeneralization; Skeptical attitude toward change

basic_info.main_problem: I feel my grandchildren do not care about me, even though I love them very much and try hard to connect with them. This feeling of Being rejected and ignored started when my grandchild was born and keeps recurring in interactions.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize these Being rejected thoughts and feelings affect my overall well-being and family relationships, so I am seeking counseling. I also hope my family can tell me this is not my fault and give me advice on how to better connect with my grandchild.
growth_experiences: When my grandchild was born, pressure rose significantly; to build a strong bond, I tried interacting and giving gifts many times, but often felt coldness and distance from them; since then each interaction easily triggers Being rejected feelings and Self-doubt, and this experience continuously affects my mood and activities in daily life.

core_beliefs: Something is wrong with me/I did wrong
I am not a good grandparent

special_situations.event: Spending time with grandchildren, when they appear cold or have no obvious response
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they do not immediately return closeness, it means I am not important and not cared about
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to gain closeness by giving gifts, increasing time together, and being more proactive
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They do not care about me/I am invisible to them

special_situations.event: After multiple efforts, still not yet seeing obvious improvement in the relationship
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If several attempts have no effect, it means it will never change
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuing to give twice as much or falling into helplessness and trying less
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I do, the result is always the same—rejection

special_situations.event: Recalling details of interactions with my grandchild when Being alone
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not good enough or did not do it right, it shows it is my fault
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuously self-reflecting and blaming myself, trying to find what I did wrong to improve
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I must have done something wrong; maybe I am not a good grandparent

special_situations.event: Occasional moments of closeness or interest
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive interaction is not genuine, just because I gave gifts
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive evidence, continuing to maintain the relationship through material means
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This closeness is not real, it is only because of the gifts

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen and cherished by grandchildren, to gain genuine closeness and attachment
core_conflict.fear: Fearing Being rejected and ignored, being seen as not important or not worthy of being loved
defense_goal: Avoiding Being rejected and maintaining a sense of connection through continued giving (gifts, proactive contact)
Avoids discussing with family to avoid being judged or seen as 'too sensitive'

object_relations.object_representation: A cold grandchild who does not care about me
object_relations.linking_affect: Sadness, Being rejected feelings, frustration and helplessness

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor asks about or emphasizes positive interaction moments with grandchildren
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting positive interactions as 'not genuine/only because of the gifts', to avoid acknowledging the possibility of being cared about
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplaying positive moments, emphasizing the role of gifts, denying positive meaning in an uncertain and doubtful tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing that the relationship cannot improve immediately or who is responsible
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Blaming the problem entirely on oneself, believing 'it is all my fault'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Repeatedly using self-blame statements, in a Depression tone, lowering self-worth, and reducing communication with family.

manifestations: Feels ignored and 'invisible' when interacting with grandchildren
Believing I am not important to my grandchild
Worrying family will not understand or will see me as 'too sensitive', making it hard to confide
outcomes: Stress about and avoidance of family interactions

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Emphasizes 'a solid bond must be built', bears enormous pressure for this
Using gifts and time to meet the inner demand of 'should be close'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-blame: 'I did wrong'/'I am not a good grandparent'
Worries about others' evaluations, thus finds it hard to discuss true feelings with family

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Believing the family may think they are 'overreacting/too sensitive', thereby avoiding expressing and seeking help

positive_force: Willing to try and cooperate with counseling (willing to start from a recent experience)
Persistently and proactively contacts grandchildren and invests time and resources (giving gifts, companionship)
Has a family support system (family to communicate with)
negative_force: Marked thought patterns: catastrophizing, overgeneralization, mind reading, predicting the future, mental filtering, negating the positive
Avoiding communication with family for fear of being judged, leading to insufficient support

target_behavior.behavior: Strong Being rejected feelings and Self-denial thinking after interacting with my grandchild
antecedent: Spending time with grandchildren, when they appear cold or have no response
Recalling interaction details and Self-doubting when Being alone
target_behavior.core_reason: Attaching self-worth excessively to the other's immediate response, activating the negative core belief ('I am not important/I am not a good grandparent')
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the pain of Being rejected, and gaining a sense of control and motivation for self-improvement through self-blame
target_behavior.consequence: Increased Low mood and helplessness, Tense family relationships, Daily activities affected

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding discussing my Being rejected and sense of loss with family
antecedent: Worries about being seen by family as 'overreacting/too sensitive'
When thinking about expressing feelings or seeking support
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing being judged and negated, tending to internalize the problem as my own fault
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential embarrassment and criticism, maintaining surface harmony
target_behavior.consequence: Lacking Social support and feedback, the problem goes uncorrected, worsening Loneliness
